topics.topic: Canonical encoding and digest algorithm for confirmation input binding
questions: Which inputs belong to each confirmed action, how are absent values, collections and text encoded and ordered, and which digest algorithm produces the binding?
What exact typed encoding, field order, treatment of absent values, and digest algorithm define the confirmation binding?
What exact canonical encoding, digest algorithm and treatment of absent, blank, ordered and structured values define equality with the confirmed inputs?

quotes:
kept as a digest of those values in a fixed order, never
   as the values themselves; a submission's inputs are bound when their digest
   equals it.
judgement.why: This is the same unchanged question about canonical confirmation-binding encoding and digest selection.

precedent.topic: Canonical confirmation-binding encoding and digest algorithm
quotes:
kept as a digest of those values in a fixed order, never
   as the values themselves; a submission's inputs are bound when their digest
   equals it.
precedent.why: The canonical byte encoding, field order, digest algorithm and representation of absent values are encoding and contract details owned by State 6.

topics.topic: Exact 30-day backup-retention deadline after erasure
questions: Because cleanup runs only daily and deletes only backups already older than 30 days, a backup can remain for almost 31 days after an erasure; is the guarantee 30 days, up to the next successful daily run after 30 days, or must deletion occur at the exact deadline?
Must a backup containing erased data disappear no later than 30 days after the erasure, or may strict age-based deletion retain it until the next daily run, almost 31 days after the erasure?
At the exact 30-day boundary, is a backup deleted or retained until the next daily run, which can keep erased data for almost 31 days?

quotes:
Third, whatever the second step did, it deletes every kept
   backup made more than 30 × 24 hours before, and every file under the kept
   prefix that cannot be read as a backup.

While the daily runs succeed, an erasure reaches the backups at most 30
   days after it, and a restore loses at most a day of changes; a failed or
   missed run lengthens both by the days until a run succeeds.
judgement.why: Strict age-based deletion during daily runs can retain a backup for almost 31 days after an erasure, contradicting the stated maximum of 30 days.

topics.topic: General well-formedness rules for configuration items
questions: What makes each location and secret well formed beyond the separately stated minimum secret length and path checks?
What exact syntax, encoding, multiplicity, and admissible-value rules make each configuration item well formed before the more specific length and path checks run?
What makes each configuration item well formed beyond the separately stated secret length and path checks?

quotes:
The checks run in one
   order and the first that fails stops the start: every item of rule 1
   present and none unknown; each well formed; each secret's length (rule 3);
   their distinctness (rule 4); the store and backup location apart (rule
   5); the backup location writable, by a probe file under the temporary
   prefix (A18 rule 5); the store opening, or made new (rule 5).
judgement.why: Exact configuration syntax, encoding, multiplicity and admissible values are schema and field-type contract details owned by State 6.

topics.topic: Linearization point for ordering concurrent owner-session requests
questions: What event establishes the total order when concurrent requests arrive together: socket receipt, completion of authentication, acquisition of a session lock, or another defined linearization point?
What event establishes the total order when concurrent requests reach different workers or become runnable simultaneously?
How is the order determined when concurrent requests reach different workers or have no observable total arrival order?

quotes:
The requests of one owner session that change its state — showing a
   confirmation step, uploading a file, a submission, a sign-out — are
   applied one at a time, in the order they reach the session: each sees the
   session as the one before left it, and other requests are not held by
   them, so a confirmation
   bound to a file a later upload replaced is refused (A16 rule 2).
judgement.divergence: One implementation orders simultaneous requests by network receipt time, while another orders them by session-lock acquisition; the owner notices which confirmation, upload, submission or sign-out wins and whether the submitted action is accepted.
judgement.why: The rule requires a total order but does not define the observable event that establishes it across concurrent workers.

topics.topic: Owner session cookie attributes, scope, transport, persistence, and deletion rules
questions: What exact cookie attributes and scope enforce this, especially since browser cookies are scoped by host and path rather than by origin or port, and is the cookie Secure on locally reached HTTP?

Which cookie attributes and scope implement “only to Registry's own origin,” including host/domain, path, SameSite policy, Secure behavior on local HTTP, persistence, and deletion on sign-out or expiry?
What exact cookie scope and transport rules apply, especially on same-host HTTP and across hosts, ports, paths and cross-site requests?

quotes:
The owner signs in with the owner credential (R0-30) and receives an owner
   session (M11), carried by a cookie that scripts cannot read, sent only over
   HTTPS when the interface is reached from another machine (R0-29), and only
   to Registry's own origin.
judgement.why: This is the same unchanged question about exact owner-session cookie attributes, scope and transport behavior.

precedent.topic: Owner-session cookie scope, attributes, and browser lifetime
quotes: The owner signs in with the owner credential (R0-30) and receives an owner session (M11), carried by a cookie that scripts cannot read, sent only over HTTPS when the interface is reached from another machine (R0-29), and only to Registry's own origin.
precedent.why: Exact cookie attributes, host/path scope and SameSite transport policy are HTTP contract and encoding details owned by State 6.

topics.topic: Policy when a scheduled backup overlaps an active backup run
questions: If the previous day's run is still active at the next 03:00 UTC, is that day's run skipped, queued to start when the old run finishes, or does it cancel or fail the old run?
If the preceding run is still active at the next 03:00 UTC, is that day's run skipped, queued to start after completion, or does the existing run count as that day's run?
If a run is still active at the next 03:00 UTC, is that day's run skipped, queued to start after the active run, or does the active run fail?

quotes:
Every day at 03:00 UTC, while Registry runs with its service tokens, it
   makes one backup run; a 03:00 that finds Registry stopped, or in an
   owner-only start (rule 9), makes no run, and none is made later in its
   place. Runs never overlap.
judgement.divergence: One implementation skips the new scheduled run when an earlier run is active, while another queues it to begin after the earlier run finishes; the owner notices different backup creation times, retained-backup sets and recovery or erasure windows.
judgement.why: The no-overlap rule does not decide what happens to a scheduled run that encounters an active run.

topics.topic: Complete set of imported facts displayed in the import mapping
questions: Must the mapping expose every imported fact the owner is approving—including object values, customer link, retained instants, pointer references, statuses and versions—or only the named summary?
Does the mapping show every imported fact of the picked projects—especially the embedded object, references, statuses and retained instants—or only the items expressly named?

quotes:
Registry
   reads it as data (A19) and answers, without changing anything, each
   project the file holds with its id and status. As the owner picks projects,
   the mapping shows for the picks only: their rooms and pointers; the display
   name and alias each will arrive under — its v1 name and no alias unless the
   owner gives others (R0-85), a name being required (A02).
judgement.why: The text expressly enumerates the project facts shown by the mapping rather than requiring every imported fact to be displayed.

topics.topic: Cryptographic authentication and tamper handling for readable backup metadata
questions: Are the readable metadata cryptographically authenticated with the encrypted store, and what prevents alteration of the instant, release, sequence number or key digest?
Is the readable metadata authenticated by the encrypted backup, and what happens when metadata is altered but the encrypted store still decrypts and passes its own integrity check?

quotes:
Each backup is encrypted with the backup key the configuration holds at its
   making (A17).
A backup cannot be read without the key it was made with.
judgement.why: This is the same unchanged question about backup metadata authentication and the authenticated-encryption envelope.

precedent.topic: Backup authenticated-encryption construction, envelope, metadata authentication, and key interpretation
quotes: Each backup is encrypted with the backup key the configuration holds at its making (A17).
A backup cannot be read without the key it was made with.
precedent.why: The algorithm, nonce, authenticated envelope, key identifier and cryptographic-version representation are encoding and file-format contract details owned by State 6.

topics.topic: Import-file digest algorithm, byte representation, and collision handling
questions: Which digest algorithm is used, and is it computed over the exact uploaded bytes or over a canonical parsed representation?
Which digest algorithm and byte representation identify the uploaded file, and what must Registry do if two different byte sequences produce the same digest?

quotes:
The mapping names
   the file by its digest.

What Registry defines is the file it accepts on import; its format belongs to States
5 and 6.
judgement.why: This is the same unchanged question about the import digest algorithm, byte representation and collision handling.

precedent.topic: Exact import-file bytes, digest algorithm, and collision handling
quotes: The mapping names the file by its digest.
What Registry defines is the file it accepts on import; its format belongs to States 5 and 6.
precedent.why: The digest algorithm, canonical byte representation and encoded digest form are format and contract details owned by State 6.

topics.topic: Namespace used to identify unknown Registry configuration items
questions: What container or namespace is examined for unknown items, so ordinary process environment variables are not silently treated either as forbidden Registry configuration or as ignored unknown configuration?
Which names are considered Registry configuration for the unknown-item check, rather than unrelated environment or process settings?

quotes:
The configuration holds exactly these items and no other: the store's
   location; the backup location and the backup key (A18); the owner
   credential; one service token for each service of A09 — PresuPro, Client
   Portal, Cabinet, Cabinet Kernel (R0-20, R0-23) — or, for an owner-only
   start, none of the four: Registry then serves the owner interface alone
   and refuses every service call (A18 rule 9).
judgement.divergence: One implementation treats every process-environment name as part of Registry configuration and refuses ordinary unrelated variables, while another checks only a Registry-specific namespace and ignores the rest; the owner notices whether the instance starts under the same host environment.
judgement.why: The texts require unknown items to stop startup but never define the configuration namespace over which that check operates.

topics.topic: Whether an empty import selection closes migration permanently
questions: May the owner confirm an empty selection, thereby writing the migration closure and permanently closing the one import without importing anything?
May the owner confirm an empty set, and if so does that empty import create the migration closure and permanently close importing?

quotes:
At the import the
owner picks any subset of its projects; the import accepts whatever the owner picks then, and the choice recorded here binds nothing.

An accepted import stores every picked project with its rooms and pointers,
   the Customers it makes, the migration closure (M10) and its one audit entry
   (M09) in one transaction.
judgement.why: An empty set is a subset, and the accepted-import rule stores the closure independently of how many projects were picked.

topics.topic: Backup encryption algorithm, nonce, key handling, and file format
questions: Which authenticated-encryption algorithm, nonce generation rule, key interpretation or derivation, and file format are required?

topics.topic: Backup metadata and validation when the store has no audit entries
questions: What value is recorded and what check is performed when the store has never written an audit entry?

topics.topic: Checks required before displaying and installing a confirmation step
questions: Which A04 checks must pass before Registry shows a confirmation step and installs its pending confirmation: only session and CSRF checks, or also existence, values, revision and lifecycle checks for the proposed action?

topics.topic: Cleanup continuation and run status after a backup deletion failure
questions: If deleting one kept file fails, does Registry stop cleanup immediately or continue attempting the remaining deletions, and how is the run classified?

topics.topic: Collision handling for generated session, CSRF, and confirmation values
questions: What happens if a newly generated session identity, CSRF value or confirmation value equals a live or previously relevant value?

topics.topic: Concurrency checks for agent-session access versions during project erasure
questions: When erasing one project moves the access versions of every session that contains it, must the erasure state and check those sessions' access versions as well as the project's revision?

topics.topic: Derivation, validation, and display of imported embedded Object data
questions: How are the required embedded Object address, optional kind and characteristics derived from the v1 project, validated, and shown in the mapping before the project is stored?

topics.topic: Deterministic first configuration failure and diagnostic naming rules
questions: When the configuration has unknown items, duplicate items, several missing items, or an equality involving two secrets, which item is the first failure and which item or items does the diagnostic name?

topics.topic: Failure stage for a project outside an agent session's project set
questions: Is failure because a project is outside the agent session's set a stage 2 authorization failure or a stage 6 lifecycle failure?

topics.topic: How expiry-triggered confirmation clearing is represented in M11
questions: Does clearing an expired confirmation count as use for M11, or must M11 explicitly include expiry-triggered clearing as a separate transition?

topics.topic: Immediate teardown requirements when an owner session expires
questions: When an expiry is first detected, must Registry immediately remove the session and all pending confirmation/upload state and clear the browser cookie, or may invalid session state and the cookie remain until later cleanup?

topics.topic: Meaning of readable backup during cleanup of older-key backups
questions: Does “read as a backup” mean that its unencrypted metadata is structurally readable, or that Registry can decrypt and validate it using the currently configured key?

topics.topic: Owner-interface display when no kept backup exists
questions: What does the owner interface show when no kept backup exists, including before the first successful run or after cleanup removes every kept file?

topics.topic: Owner-interface treatment of malformed or undecryptable kept backups
questions: Before the next cleanup run, how does the interface treat a kept-prefix file with malformed or tampered metadata, or a kept backup that cannot be opened with an available key?

topics.topic: Previously uploaded file retention after upload-time refusal
questions: Do all upload-time refusals preserve the session's previously uploaded file, or only the specifically named too-large and unreadable cases?

topics.topic: Reporting dependent authentication checks when the owner session is invalid
questions: When the owner session is invalid, Registry cannot determine whether supplied CSRF and confirmation values are bound to that session; should it report only the session failure or also report the dependent checks as failures?

topics.topic: Required ownership and permission checks for secret files
questions: Is Registry required to verify ownership and permissions of a file holding secrets before serving, or is this entirely an unchecked host-administration guarantee?

topics.topic: Scheduling rule when startup occurs exactly at 03:00 UTC
questions: If Registry starts or finishes configuration checks at exactly 03:00 UTC, what determines whether that day's run occurs?

topics.topic: Store-history identity and boundary after restoration
questions: What identifies the beginning and identity of a store history when Registry cannot detect a restore and neither the store nor backup metadata carries a history identity?

topics.topic: Temporary state retained after refusal of an import confirmation
questions: After refusal, which temporary facts remain: the uploaded file, mapping choices, pending confirmation, or none of them?

topics.topic: Timing and failure behavior for cleanup of a leftover startup probe
questions: At what startup step is a leftover probe identified and removed, and does inability to remove it fail the next start or merely leave it for a backup run?

topics.topic: Version fact stored for confirmed actions without revisions or access versions
questions: What revision-or-access-version fact does the OwnerSession carry for confirmed actions that have neither, particularly the import and erasure of old audit entries?

topics.topic: Whether an accepted import upload stores or replaces session upload state
questions: Does an accepted upload change owner-session state by storing or replacing the uploaded file, or must the upload be observational only?

topics.topic: Whether stage 3 reports all missing records or stops at dependency failures
questions: Must Registry look up and disclose every missing named record in one answer, or may a dependency such as a missing pointer or project stop lookups whose identities can only be derived from it?
